newsitem.title: ITALY: Crucial talks start on Italian metalworkers pay.
newsitem.headline: Crucial talks start on Italian metalworkers pay.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi began a crucial meeting with trade unions and industry leaders on Monday that he hopes will resolve a bitter and protracted pay dispute in Italy's engineering and metalworking industry.

Prodi called the talks with leaders of the three main labour confederations and employers' group Confindustria last Friday after signs that the six-month-old battle over wage rises for 1.7 million workers was close to a settlement.
None of the participants made any comment to reporters on their way into the talks at Prodi's office.
Industry sources said that if successful, they would be followed by negotiations between sectoral unions and the industry group, Federmeccanica.
The engineering and metalworking industry accounts for 40 percent of Italian industrial output and any settlement is expected to set the time for pay deals in other sectors.

"I think all the elements are in place to get ready to sign," Prodi said on Sunday on the eve of the talks, which were also being attended by Labour Minister Tiziano Treu and Industry Minister Pierluigi Bersani.
